A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CheXGenBench and its 11-model MIMIC-CXR benchmark. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original fidelity, privacy, classification, report-generation, and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds augmentation, segmentation, privacy-reference, and supplementary experimental findings.

M1.justification: v4 removes the auxiliary SynthCheX-75K production workflow involving extended Sana training and HealthGPT quality filtering (v3 Section 4 and Appendix F). The core generative architectures and benchmark pipeline remain. Newly documenting rsLoRA does not establish that the retained experiments switched training methods.

E1.justification: v4 adds pixel-level clavicle segmentation, substantially extending the previous classification and report-generation utility coverage. It uses pseudolabeled MIMIC-CXR images; no additional evaluated source dataset or external domain is introduced.

E2.justification: The 11-model roster and original standalone comparisons remain. v4 adds real longitudinal radiographs as a privacy reference baseline. Its new RRG augmentation comparison evaluates SD V1-4, SD V1-5, RadEdit, Pixart Sigma, and Sana; the remaining generators still appear in the retained RRG experiment.

E3.justification: v4 adds classification training with 20K real plus 20K synthetic images and RRG training from scratch with 50K real plus 20K synthetic images, while retaining the earlier settings in Appendix A.7. Segmentation uses U-Net, pseudolabeled clavicles, and 3K real images augmented with 3K or 7K synthetic images. GREENScore and RaTEScore expand RRG evaluation.

E4.justification: v4 adds LoRA-placement ablations, synthetic-volume scaling analyses, qualitative texture comparisons, and reported pathology-stratified privacy findings. It revises fidelity–utility correlation analysis to cover augmentation and segmentation. The Sana 20-versus-50-epoch analysis is removed, while caption, encoder, and LoRA-rank ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten generation seeds per prompt for the 2,000-image privacy evaluation. The same plus/minus reporting appears in v3 Table 6b and v4 Table 19b. No new repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported; changed correlation coefficients are result changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 remain numerically unchanged, and the original utility results move to Tables 15–16, with additional RRG metrics. New results include augmentation AUCs, segmentation Dice scores, a real-data Re-ID baseline of 0.59, and scaling/placement findings. Under the new RRG setting, Sana obtains BLEU-4 11.28 versus its real-only control’s 10.29; this is not a same-setting improvement over v3. Extended-training results are removed.

T1.justification: The privacy definitions and aggregation equations from v3 Section 2.3 and Appendix I are retained in v4 Section 2.3. Their relocation introduces no substantive mathematical change. The new texture–topology discussion is conceptual rather than a formal theory or proof.

C1.justification: v4 removes SynthCheX-75K as a headline contribution and expands the claimed utility suite to include segmentation. It foregrounds classification augmentation benefits and the texture–topology research challenge. The central claim of a unified fidelity, privacy, and utility benchmark remains.

C2.justification: v4 introduces texture–topology and forgetting explanations for downstream behavior, interprets synthetic privacy risk relative to real radiographs, and argues for pathology-aware privacy assessment. It also asserts reliability across dataset sizes and adds contamination and deployment discussions. Earlier explicit caveats about single-dataset evaluation and absent human assessment are removed.

D1.justification: v4 documents rsLoRA, alpha equal to rank, BioViL-T cosine similarity, segmentation pseudolabeling, and the U-Net learning rate. Conversely, SynthCheX-75K’s filtering prompt, data card, licensing, and access documentation disappear. Release statements now emphasize code, splits, annotations, and generated outputs from all baselines. Existing T2I learning rates and hardware descriptions remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations supporting CLIPScore, rsLoRA, U-Net, segmentation pseudolabeling, GREENScore, and RaTEScore, alongside several introductory citations. HealthGPT, TTT-Bench, and SynFAC-Edit references are removed. The broader positioning against fragmented medical-generation evaluation remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are extensively rewritten, introductory criticisms become a numbered list, and the dataset section is replaced by a texture–topology discussion. Original utility experiments move into reorganized appendices, privacy equations move into the main text, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a substantially different journal layout, reformats tables, and adds segmentation, augmentation, scaling, and LoRA-placement displays plus a real-versus-synthetic radiograph panel. Original utility tables and the caption histogram relocate. The pathology-frequency chart and extended-Sana-training plots are removed, although pathology counts remain tabulated.

improvement.justification: v4 usefully extends v3’s utility evaluation with augmentation, segmentation, and additional ablations. However, new Table 10 assigns RadEdit and Flux the same segmentation rank despite Dice scores of 0.667 and 0.562 in Table 5, weakening its correlation-based interpretation. It also asserts dataset-size-independent metric reliability without a supporting test and removes detailed SynthCheX-75K documentation. These substantive gains and reliability/documentation losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
